children: New members including SoftBank Corp. and Crusoe join the cloud native community to help build cost-efficient, sovereign infrastructure
SHANGHAI, Sept. 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --

, which builds sustainable ecosystems for cloud native software, today announced the addition of nine new Silver members, including telecommunications leader SoftBank Corp. and AI infrastructure provider Crusoe, reinforcing the continued momentum of cloud native adoption across industries and further strengthening the foundation's global community. This cohort, spanning telecommunications, AI infrastructure, cloud hosting, infrastructure efficiency, autonomous code optimization, sovereign infrastructure, and open source data retrieval, joins the nearly 800 members and over 300,000 contributors across more than 250 projects and 190 countries in the cloud native ecosystem.

"With the shift from AI experimentation to 24/7 production inference at scale, the challenge is about getting more from the infrastructure organizations already have rather than adding more compute," said Jonathan Bryce, executive director of CNCF. "Open source communities are building the orchestration, observability and infrastructure layers needed to use those resources more efficiently. These new members bring expertise across the stack and strengthen the community working to make production AI infrastructure more efficient and accessible."

As organizations transition AI workloads from training to inference, platform teams face rising demands for operational efficiency, data sovereignty, and resource optimization. CNCF's newest members reflect that shift, bringing domain expertise and technology built for production-scale AI.
New Silver Members
The following organizations have recently joined CNCF as Silver Members:

CodeVisionary

Crusoe

Crusoe's vertically integrated model is purpose-built for AI infrastructure – from energy to compute to cloud. Crusoe Cloud is engineered for AI training, inference, and high-performance computing workloads, offering GPU-powered managed inference services and infrastructure-as-a-service with intelligent orchestration.
DHH

Through its portfolio of brands, it provides scalable, secure, and high-performance hosting, cloud, artificial intelligence, and connectivity solutions to businesses of all sizes. DHH is deeply rooted in the open source community, believing that the best technology is built through collaboration and transparency.
Infino AI

SoftBank Corp.

(TOKYO: 9434) operates telecommunications and IT businesses in Japan and globally. Building on its strong business foundation, SoftBank Corp. aims to activate the potential of AI across its businesses and drive implementation in line with its "Activate AI for Society" growth strategy. While further growing its telecom business, SoftBank is expanding its AI computing infrastructure and AI and Cloud service businesses, aiming to become a provider of Next-generation Social Infrastructure.
Valarian Technologies Ltd
builds sovereign digital infrastructure by deploying AI on hardened Kubernetes to keep control of data, agents, and business at scale.
About the Newest Silver End User Member
CNCF also welcomes its newest Silver End User Member, an organization that actively uses cloud native technologies to drive digital transformation:
Legora

is building the OS for the world's legal work: collaborative AI for exceptional lawyers. Legora's multi-region AI platform runs on Kubernetes and the CNCF ecosystem, including Argo CD, Kargo, Crossplane, Cilium, and Kyverno. With engineering offices in Stockholm, New York, and London, the company is growing its platform and infrastructure teams to contribute back to CNCF projects.

CNCF Silver Members receive various benefits valued at over $300,000 USD, including training and educational subscriptions, event sponsorship discounts, access to The Linux Foundation's legal resources, opportunities to join project working groups, and more.
To learn more about becoming a Silver Member, visit: https://www.cncf.io/about/join/silver
About Cloud Native Computing Foundation

Cloud native computing empowers organizations to build and run scalable applications with an open source software stack in public, private, and hybrid clouds. The Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) hosts critical components of the global technology infrastructure, including Kubernetes, Prometheus, and Envoy. CNCF brings together the industry's top developers, end users, and vendors and runs the largest open source developer conferences in the world. Supported by nearly 800 members, including the world's largest cloud computing and software companies, as well as over 200 innovative startups, CNCF is part of the nonprofit Linux Foundation. For more information, please visit www.cncf.io.
